chapters.title: Living hope and a call to holiness

parts.text: Peter greets the scattered strangers as God’s elect and praises him for new birth into living hope through Jesus’ resurrection. An unfading inheritance awaits those kept by God’s power through faith. Present trials test faith more precious than gold and lead toward praise at Christ’s appearing. The salvation now announced was searched out by prophets who foretold Christ’s sufferings and subsequent glory.

The readers must set their hope on the coming grace, live soberly and holily, and fear the Father who judges impartially. Their redemption cost Christ’s precious blood, not perishable wealth. Having obeyed the truth and been born again through God’s enduring word, they must love one another sincerely and fervently.

chapters.title: A spiritual house and conduct worthy of Christ

parts.text: Peter calls the readers to put away malice and deceit and desire the word like newborn children. Coming to Christ, the living stone rejected by men but chosen by God, they are built into a spiritual house and holy priesthood. He is precious to believers but a stumbling stone to the disobedient. As God’s chosen people, they should declare his praises and live honourably among the Gentiles.

They are to submit to authorities for the Lord’s sake, honour everyone, love the brethren, and fear God. Servants should endure unjust suffering patiently. Christ’s sinless suffering provides their example: he did not retaliate but entrusted himself to the righteous Judge. Bearing their sins, he brings wandering sheep back to their Shepherd.

chapters.title: Honour, a good conscience, and Christ’s victory

parts.text: Wives are urged to honour their husbands through chaste conduct and the inward beauty of a meek spirit. Husbands must dwell with understanding and honour their wives as fellow heirs of life’s grace. All should show compassion, bless rather than retaliate, restrain evil speech, and pursue peace under God’s watchful care.

Suffering for righteousness is preferable to wrongdoing. The readers should explain their hope with meekness and fear while keeping a good conscience. Christ suffered once, the just for the unjust, to bring them to God. The passage recalls his preaching to spirits in prison who disobeyed in Noah’s days. Peter says baptism now saves through Christ’s resurrection, distinguishing it from bodily washing and connecting it with a good conscience toward God. Christ now rules above angels and powers.

chapters.title: Live for God and endure the fiery trial

parts.text: The readers must adopt Christ’s resolve in suffering and live for God’s will rather than former lusts and excesses. Those who malign their changed conduct will answer to the Judge of living and dead. The gospel’s preaching to the dead is linked with life according to God in the spirit. With the end near, he urges sober prayer, fervent love, willing hospitality, and faithful use of gifts so God is glorified through Jesus Christ.

Fiery trials should not seem strange. Sharing Christ’s sufferings brings hope of joy when his glory appears. They must not suffer as evildoers, but should glorify God if they suffer as Christians. Judgment begins at God’s house, and those suffering according to his will should entrust their souls to the faithful Creator while doing good.

Peter addresses the elders as a fellow elder and witness of Christ’s sufferings. They should shepherd God’s flock willingly, without greed or domination, becoming examples until the chief Shepherd appears with an unfading crown. Younger believers should submit to elders, and everyone should practice humility. God resists pride but gives grace to the humble, who may cast their cares upon him because he cares for them.

The readers must stay alert and resist the devil steadfastly in faith, remembering that believers elsewhere share their sufferings. Peter asks the God of grace to strengthen and establish them after suffering. He closes with assurances of true grace, greetings, and peace to those in Christ.
